title: Getting Started with ccreds
text: generate data censored-covariate regression model \(n = 200\) observations \(p = 30\) features. Response-variable model: \[y_i = \beta_0 + \alpha x_i + \pmb{\beta}^\top \mathbf{z}_i + \varepsilon_i, \quad \varepsilon_i \sim N(0, \sigma^2)\] Censored-covariate model: \[X_i \mid \mathbf{z}_i \sim \chi^2(\mu_i), \quad \mu_i = \exp(\gamma_0 + \pmb{\gamma}^\top \mathbf{z}_i)\] set \(\pmb{\beta}\) \(\pmb{\gamma}\) sparse partially overlapping support, features affect response, affect censored covariate, affect . set censoring rate approximately 50%.
code: set.seed(2026)  n <- 200 p <- 30  # Correlated features (AR(0.5) structure) rho <- 0.5 Sigma <- 9*toeplitz(rho^(0:(p - 1))) z <- mvrnorm(n = n, mu = rep(0, p), Sigma = Sigma)  # True parameters beta_0 <- 5 alpha <- 10 beta <- c(4, 4, 2, rep(0, p-5), -2, -4) sigma_sq <- 100  gamma_0 <- 2 gamma <- c(0.04, 0.04, 0.02, 0.02, rep(0, p-4))  # Generate the censored covariate x x_mean <- exp(cbind(1, z) %*% c(gamma_0, gamma)) |> drop() x <- rchisq(n, df = x_mean)  # Generate censoring times to achieve ~50% censoring compute_c_mean <- function(censoring_rate, x_mean) {   f <- function(c_mean) {     1 - pbeta(0.5, x_mean / 2, c_mean / 2) - censoring_rate   }   uniroot(f, lower = 1e-12, upper = 1000)$root } c_mean <- vapply(x_mean, \(m) compute_c_mean(0.5, m), numeric(1)) cens <- rchisq(n, df = c_mean)  # Generate response e <- rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = sqrt(sigma_sq)) y <- cbind(1, x, z) %*% c(beta_0, alpha, beta) + e  # Observed covariate and censoring indicator w <- pmin(x, cens) d <- as.numeric(x <= cens)  # Assemble the data frame in the format ccreds() expects z_df <- as.data.frame(z) colnames(z_df) <- paste0("z", 1:p) dat <- tibble(   case = 1:n,   y = drop(y),   w = w,   d = d ) |>   bind_cols(z_df)  dat #> # A tibble: 200 × 34 #>     case      y     w     d     z1      z2     z3       z4     z5      z6    z7 #>    <int>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> #>  1     1  -6.33  3.72     0 -3.80  -3.24   -1.85  -0.0231  -3.34  -1.43    4.59 #>  2     2  23.5   3.46     1 -4.53  -0.0690 -3.93   2.98     7.22   5.55    2.89 #>  3     3  -3.79  2.85     0  0.698 -7.17   -6.90  -1.07     2.17  -1.17   -1.55 #>  4     4  -2.67  3.63     1 -5.12  -0.847  -0.182 -4.16    -2.85  -4.43   -4.50 #>  5     5 159.    7.11     0  3.32  -0.365  -1.42  -4.99     0.946  0.200   2.99 #>  6     6  95.5   3.86     0  1.23  -1.26    3.49   0.00796  3.45   0.0594  2.18 #>  7     7   5.01  4.32     1 -3.31   2.51    3.72   4.71     3.38   4.61    3.32 #>  8     8 173.    6.34     0  1.74   0.959   0.681  1.35     4.43   5.00    2.85 #>  9     9 226.   11.2      0  5.11   4.75    2.92  -0.642    0.462 -1.39   -5.84 #> 10    10  54.8   8.13     1  1.18  -1.45    2.00  -0.840   -0.143  2.43    2.77 #> # text: Use extract_fit() retrieve fitted model. default rule = "min" selects \((\lambda_1, \lambda_2)\) pair minimises CV_MAE_y. rule = "1se" alternative selects parsimonious model whose CV_MAE_y within one standard error minimum. can inspect first estimated coefficients compare truth:

title: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection
text: ccreds R package performing Censored-Covariate Regression Dual Selection. ccreds allows users fit penalised censored-covariate regression models two separate L1 penalties — one selecting features associated response variable one selecting features associated censored covariate. Tuning parameters selected via cross-validation. Functions producing visual diagnostics cross-validation heat maps, coefficient paths, plotting estimated densities, provided.

title: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection
text: Install GitHub : using Windows:
code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("rajan-shankar/ccreds") # install.packages("devtools") devtools::install_github("rajan-shankar/ccreds")

title: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection
text: main function ccreds(). Input data must data frame columns order: output tibble one row per (lambda_1, lambda_2) pair, containing cross-validation metrics full model fit. Use extract_fit() retrieve best model: parallel computation lambda grid: requires future furrr packages.
code: library(ccreds)  results <- ccreds(   data = my_data,   lambda_1s = c(0.01, 0.1, 1),   lambda_2s = c(0.01, 0.1, 1),   k = 5 ) # Minimum CV MAE rule (default) fit <- extract_fit(results)  # One-standard-error rule (most parsimonious model within 1 SE of the minimum) fit <- extract_fit(results, rule = "1se")  fit$beta_0    # Intercept (beta_0) fit$alpha     # Coefficient of censored covariate x (alpha) fit$beta      # Feature coefficients for y (beta vector) fit$sigma_sq  # Error variance (sigma^2) fit$gamma_0   # Intercept for x model (gamma_0) fit$gamma     # Feature coefficients for x (gamma vector) results <- ccreds(   data = my_data,   lambda_1s = c(0.01, 0.1, 1),   lambda_2s = c(0.01, 0.1, 1),   cores = 4 )

title: ccreds: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection — ccreds-package
text: Implements penalised observed-data log-likelihood method feature selection censored-covariate regression models. Uses two separate L1 penalties select features associated response variable features associated censored covariate, via Expectation-Minimisation (EM) algorithm. Tuning parameters chosen cross-validation.

title: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection — ccreds
code: ccreds(   data,   lambda_1s = 10^seq(-4, 0, length.out = 9),   lambda_2s = 10^seq(-4, 0, length.out = 9),   force_active_beta = integer(0),   force_active_gamma = integer(0),   k = 5,   cores = 1 )

title: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection — ccreds
text: data data frame columns order: case (integer ID), y (response), w (observed value x censoring time), d (censoring indicator: 1 = observed, 0 = censored), z1, z2, ..., zp (features). lambda_1s Numeric vector candidate values \(\lambda_1\), penalty \(\pmb{\beta}\). lambda_2s Numeric vector candidate values \(\lambda_2\), penalty \(\pmb{\gamma}\). force_active_beta Integer vector feature indices (referring z column numbers) penalised \(\pmb{\beta}\). Default integer(0). force_active_gamma Integer vector feature indices penalised \(\pmb{\gamma}\). Default integer(0). k Number cross-validation folds. Default 5. cores Number parallel workers. greater 1, uses future furrr parallel computation. Default 1.

title: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection — ccreds
text: tibble one row per \((\lambda_1, \lambda_2)\) pair columns: lambda_1, lambda_2 tuning parameter values. full_fit list containing fitted model full data, elements: beta_0 Intercept \(\beta_0\). alpha Coefficient \(\alpha\) censored covariate \(x\). beta Feature coefficient vector \(\pmb{\beta}\) length \(p\). sigma_sq Error variance \(\sigma^2\). gamma_0 Intercept \(\gamma_0\). gamma Feature coefficient vector \(\pmb{\gamma}\) length \(p\). beta_selected Number non-zero entries \(\hat{\pmb{\beta}}\) (excluding forced-active features). gamma_selected Number non-zero entries \(\hat{\pmb{\gamma}}\) (excluding forced-active features). iterations Number EM iterations convergence. CV_MAE_y Cross-validated mean absolute error \(y\). CV_MAE_y_SE Standard error CV_MAE_y across folds. CV_MAE_x Cross-validated mean absolute error \(x\) (computed complete observations ). CV_MAE_x_SE Standard error CV_MAE_x across folds. time Elapsed time fitting lambda pair.

title: Censored-Covariate Regression with Dual Selection — ccreds
text: censored-covariate regression model consists two components: Response-variable model: $$y_i = \beta_0 + \alpha x_i + \pmb{\beta}^\top   \mathbf{z}_i + \varepsilon_i, \quad \varepsilon_i \sim N(0,   \sigma^2)$$ Censored-covariate model: $$X_i \mid \mathbf{z}_i \sim \chi^2(\mu_i), \quad \mu_i =   \exp(\gamma_0 + \pmb{\gamma}^\top \mathbf{z}_i)$$ \(\beta_0\) \(\gamma_0\) intercepts, \(\alpha\) coefficient censored covariate \(x\), \(\pmb{\beta}\) \(\pmb{\gamma}\) feature coefficient vectors subject \(L_1\) penalisation.

what: Extract a fitted model from ccreds results — extract_fit
title: Extract a fitted model from ccreds results — extract_fit
text: Extracts fitted model ccreds() results tibble using either minimum CV MAE rule one-standard-error (1-SE) rule.

title: Extract a fitted model from ccreds results — extract_fit
code: extract_fit(results, rule = c("min", "1se"))

title: Extract a fitted model from ccreds results — extract_fit
text: results tibble returned ccreds(). rule Character string specifying selection rule. "min" (default) selects \((\lambda_1, \lambda_2)\) pair smallest CV_MAE_y. "1se" selects parsimonious model whose CV_MAE_y within one standard error minimum — , among models CV_MAE_y <= min(CV_MAE_y) + CV_MAE_y_SE minimum, model fewest total selected features chosen.

title: Extract a fitted model from ccreds results — extract_fit
text: named list containing fitted model parameters: beta_0 Intercept \(\beta_0\). alpha Coefficient \(\alpha\) censored covariate \(x\). beta Feature coefficient vector \(\pmb{\beta}\) length \(p\). sigma_sq Error variance \(\sigma^2\). gamma_0 Intercept \(\gamma_0\). gamma Feature coefficient vector \(\pmb{\gamma}\) length \(p\). beta_selected Number non-zero entries \(\hat{\pmb{\beta}}\). gamma_selected Number non-zero entries \(\hat{\pmb{\gamma}}\). iterations Number EM iterations convergence.

title: Extract a fitted model from ccreds results — extract_fit
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ results <- ccreds(data, lambda_1s, lambda_2s)  # Best model by minimum CV MAE fit <- extract_fit(results)  # Most parsimonious model within 1 SE of the minimum fit_1se <- extract_fit(results, rule = "1se")  fit$beta fit$gamma } # }

title: Plot coefficient paths — plot_coefficient_paths
text: Shows estimated feature coefficients \(\pmb{\beta}\) \(\pmb{\gamma}\) change corresponding penalty parameter varies. component = "beta", plot varies \(\lambda_1\) holding \(\lambda_2\) fixed, vice versa component = "gamma".

title: Plot coefficient paths — plot_coefficient_paths
code: plot_coefficient_paths(   results,   component = c("beta", "gamma"),   lambda_fixed = NULL,   feature_names = NULL,   highlight = TRUE )

title: Plot coefficient paths — plot_coefficient_paths
text: results tibble returned ccreds(). component Either "beta" "gamma". lambda_fixed value penalty hold constant plotted penalty varies. component = "beta", fixes \(\lambda_2\); component = "gamma", fixes \(\lambda_1\). NULL (default), uses value minimum CV_MAE_y model. feature_names Optional character vector length \(p\) giving display names features. NULL, uses z1, z2, etc. highlight Logical; TRUE (default), highlights features non-zero minimum-CV model adds dashed vertical line chosen penalty value.

title: Plot coefficient paths — plot_coefficient_paths
text: ggplot object.

title: Plot coefficient paths — plot_coefficient_paths
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ results <- ccreds(data, lambda_1s, lambda_2s) plot_coefficient_paths(results, "beta") plot_coefficient_paths(results, "gamma",   feature_names = c("age", "weight", "height") ) } # }

title: Plot predictive densities — plot_density
text: Plots joint density \(f(y, x \mid \mathbf{z})\) filled contour, , y_given supplied, overlays marginal density \(f(x \mid \mathbf{z})\) conditional density \(f(x \mid \mathbf{z}, y)\) specific value \(y\).

title: Plot predictive densities — plot_density
code: plot_density(   fit,   z,   x_range = NULL,   y_range = NULL,   y_given = NULL,   n_grid = 200 )

title: Plot predictive densities — plot_density
text: fit single fitted model list (e.g. one element full_fit column ccreds() output), containing beta_0, alpha, beta, sigma_sq, gamma_0, gamma. z Numeric vector feature values (length \(p\)). x_range Numeric vector length 2 giving range \(x\) values plot. Default computed chi-squared distribution implied model. y_range Numeric vector length 2 giving range \(y\) values (used joint contour plot). Default computed model. y_given Optional scalar. supplied, produces density overlay \(f(x \mid \mathbf{z})\) \(f(x \mid \mathbf{z}, y = y_{given})\) instead joint contour. n_grid Number grid points per axis. Default 200.

title: Plot predictive densities — plot_density
text: ggplot object.

title: Plot predictive densities — plot_density
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ results <- ccreds(data, lambda_1s, lambda_2s) fit <- results$full_fit[[1]] z_vals <- c(0.5, -0.3, 1.2)  # Joint density contour plot_density(fit, z_vals)  # Marginal vs conditional density of x given y = 60 plot_density(fit, z_vals, y_given = 60) } # }
